sections.h2: What is different about selling in Wheaton?
sections.html:
Wheaton adds a city transfer stamp to every sale, and the buyer pays for it. The city also wants the seller's final utility bill settled before the stamp is issued, so the two sides of a closing depend on each other. Wheaton is the DuPage County seat and sits about 25 miles west of Chicago, in Milton and Winfield Townships.

The same rules apply whether the house is listed, sold privately or bought for cash as-is. What changes is who files the stamp application and how early the final water reading is booked.

The stamp costs $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration, taken from line 11 of the Illinois MyDec PTAX-203 declaration, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. The buyer, called the grantee, buys it. Illinois collects its own tax too, at half a dollar for each $500 of declared value (35 ILCS 200/31-10).

The city's Finance Department accepts stamp requests four ways:

  • Online through the transfer stamp portal, after creating an account.
  • By email to finance@wheaton.il.us.
  • By UPS or FedEx to the Finance Department at 303 W. Wesley St., Wheaton, IL 60187.
  • In person at City Hall, first floor.

Paper filings need a signed stamp application, a copy of the completed PTAX-203 or the deed, and a completed city utility account application form.

Most Wheaton sales are non-exempt because they carry money. The full list of exempt deeds sits in City Code Chapter 66, Article VII, Section 66-190, and these are common ones.

Common exemptions from the Wheaton transfer stamp
Exempt situationNote
Transfer to or from a trustStill needs a $0 value stamp
Actual consideration under $100.00Same $0 stamp
Property acquired by or from a governmental bodyDocumentation required
Buyer sold a Wheaton primary home and is buying a new principal residence in WheatonExemption 13
Buyer is the natural or adopted child of a sellerExemption 14

An exempt stamp carries a $25 administrative fee and needs a signed, notarized deed. Since October 1, 2025 Wheaton no longer pays transfer tax refunds. Situations that once qualified for a refund are now handled as exemptions when the stamp is bought, so supporting documents must be ready on the closing timeline.

sections.h2: Seller duties before the stamp is issued
sections.html:
Call the city 5 to 7 days before closing to book a final water reading, at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us. The final bill, or an estimate of it, then has to be paid in full. The city also checks for other unpaid charges.

  • Water, sanitary sewer and stormwater utility fees.
  • Inspection fees.
  • Building permit fees.
  • Property maintenance fines.

Because building permit fees and property maintenance fines are on the list, ask the city for a balance on your account a couple of weeks ahead and clear anything outstanding before the contract date.

Wheaton is an upper-priced market. The median home value is $455,700, median gross rent is $1,799 a month and median household income is $120,008. Owners live in 71.7% of the housing, across 19,588 households averaging 2.54 people. Population is estimated at 54,065 for July 2025, essentially level with the 2020 count of 53,970.

Monthly costs for owners average $2,764 with a mortgage and $1,138 without one, and 86.4% of residents had the same address a year earlier. Little turnover means few comparable sales, so pricing a house takes care.

sections.h2: Property taxes for a Wheaton seller
sections.html:
Wheaton parcels are billed by DuPage County. Taxes arrive a year behind, with bills mailed in spring and installments recently falling on June 1 and September 1. The general homestead and senior exemptions are each $8,000 on the county's current notice, and you should confirm both appear on your bill. For assessed value questions, the county treasurer points owners to the local assessor's number printed on the bill.

On the settlement statement the title company divides the unpaid tax for the year. State law also requires sellers of one to four residential units to hand over a completed disclosure report before a contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20). For a rough house, that report is where known problems get written down.

sections.h2: What can slow down a Wheaton closing?
sections.html:
Most delays come from the utility step or from a missing exemption record. The city will not issue the transfer stamp until the final utility bill is paid, so a late call to the utility office can hold up the stamp and the recording that follows.

  • Booking the final water reading later than the 5 to 7 day window the city requests.
  • Forgetting that the buyer, not the seller, submits the PTAX-203 copy and the utility account application.
  • Claiming an exemption without a notarized deed or supporting documents.
  • Leaving building permit fees or property maintenance fines unpaid.
  • Counting on a refund after closing, which the city no longer issues.

Sellers who need to leave quickly, such as an estate heir or an owner relocating for work, should line up these items with the title company the week the contract is signed.

Once the contract is signed, call the title company and ask who is filing the PTAX-203 and who is sending the stamp application. Book the final water reading inside the 5 to 7 day window, and settle any permit fees or maintenance fines with the city. Get your payoff letter from any lender.

On closing day you sign the deed, the lender is paid from your proceeds, and the stamped deed goes to DuPage County for recording. A cash buyer has no loan approval to wait on, so the stamp and the utility bill are usually the last items standing between you and the keys. Save the final utility receipt, since the city needs it before the stamp issues, and keep a copy of the stamped deed for your records.

Most of Wheaton lies in Community Unit School District 200, feeding Wheaton North and Wheaton Warrenville South high schools. The northeast corner is in Glen Ellyn District 41 and one elementary school in the southeast belongs to District 89. The Union Pacific West Line runs through downtown, where the Wheaton Center apartment complex is a recognizable landmark. Mention the school district and the train when you describe the house.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wheaton transfer stamp, the buyer or the seller?
faqs.a: The buyer, also called the grantee, buys the stamp. The seller's job is to book the final water reading and pay the final utility bill, because the city will not issue the stamp until that bill is settled.

faqs.q: What is the Wheaton transfer stamp rate?
faqs.a: It is $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration from line 11 of the PTAX-203, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. Exempt deeds still need a $0 stamp and a $25 administrative fee.

faqs.q: How early should I schedule the final water reading in Wheaton?
faqs.a: Call 5 to 7 days before closing. The city's Finance Department takes requests at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us, and the final bill must be paid before the stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Did Wheaton stop refunding transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes, as of October 1, 2025. Buyers who would have qualified for a refund, such as a Wheaton homeowner moving to another Wheaton home or a child buying from a parent, now claim Exemption 13 or 14 when they apply for the stamp.

faqs.q: Which county handles property tax for Wheaton?
faqs.a: DuPage County. Its treasurer mails one bill with two installment coupons, and the county bills a year in arrears. Call the treasurer for the current due dates.
